verdict.rationale: Gazebo documents programmatic control of a running simulation. Gazebo Transport offers socket-based publish/subscribe messaging plus service calls and discovery, so users can drive a server, including remote or headless ones, from outside. It can also be embedded as a C++ library, with standalone example programs, and controlled through extensive command-line tools. The 404s for OpenAPI and llms.txt only show there is no web-style spec, which does not contradict the native transport and library APIs. Missing for 10: detailed API reference coverage (specific services and message types for controlling the sim), evidence of non-C++ bindings such as Python, a machine-readable API spec, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven use.
